meta.title: Evaluating Agentic Workflows
meta.thesis: Evaluating Agentic Workflows is practical when learners can apply it to this concrete case: A multi-step ticket agent must be judged on tool choices, state updates, and final answer quality. By the end, they should be able to build or review agent workflow evaluation trace with step-level assertions, measure task success with correct intermediate actions, and catch the failure where the final answer looks right while the agent took unsafe or wasteful steps.

blocks.title: Why Evaluating Agentic Workflows matters here

spans.text: Problem statement: A multi-step ticket agent must be judged on tool choices, state updates, and final answer quality. The learner's job is not to memorize Evaluating Agentic Workflows; it is to decide what to build or change, what evidence the system may use, and how to tell whether the change improved task success with correct intermediate actions.

Running case: agent workflow evaluation trace with step-level assertions. We will keep this same case through the lesson so each idea has a job: frame the problem, explain the mechanism, choose a design, test the implementation, and decide what to do next.

Before reading on, predict: if the final answer looks right while the agent took unsafe or wasteful steps, where would you look first - the input, the state or data, the model boundary, the validation check, or the release process?
The lesson skips definition-drilling and spends its effort on edge cases: state boundaries, hidden coupling, observability gaps, and the evidence that would change a production decision.

items.text: Product framing: Evaluating Agentic Workflows matters when it changes a user-visible decision, release gate, or operational workflow.
Engineering framing: Evaluating Agentic Workflows matters when it changes data, state, prompts, model behavior, tools, schemas, traces, or runtime constraints.
Validation framing: the lesson is not complete until the team can measure task success with correct intermediate actions on examples that resemble the real workload.

blocks.title: Fully worked example: agent workflow evaluation trace with step-level assertions

spans.text: Scenario: A multi-step ticket agent must be judged on tool choices, state updates, and final answer quality. The team wants to improve task success with correct intermediate actions, but it has already seen this failure: the final answer looks right while the agent took unsafe or wasteful steps.
Here is the worked artifact at design-review depth: concrete enough to inspect, small enough to build as a thin slice.
Complete worked artifact

items.text: Release change: a prompt or workflow update makes answers warmer, but the team must prove it did not lose required facts, citations, refusals, or safe tool behavior.

Artifact: agent workflow evaluation trace with step-level assertions. It includes golden inputs, expected behaviors, assertions, failure labels, owner, and the release gate for task success with correct intermediate actions.
Worked output: case refund-policy-1 must include "30 days" and "invoice id", must not promise guaranteed approval, and must cite the refund policy source.

spans.text: Complete AI-assistant prompt for this artifact

Role: evaluation lead. Context: A multi-step ticket agent must be judged on tool choices, state updates, and final answer quality. Task: build the smallest golden test pack for Evaluating Agentic Workflows. Include happy path, edge case, refusal or escalation case, and one regression tied to "the final answer looks right while the agent took unsafe or wasteful steps". Output: {cases, assertions, pass_fail_gate, owner}.
Why this is richer than a definition
The example ties Evaluating Agentic Workflows to a specific input, output, decision, failure mode, and metric. That is the move you should repeat when applying the lesson to your own system.

blocks.title: Mechanism: the mechanism in the running case

spans.text: Mechanism opens the machinery behind Evaluating Agentic Workflows. In the running case, the important question is: what exactly changes between the user's request and the final output?
Mechanism means turning subjective quality into repeatable cases, assertions, rubrics, and release gates.
Two framings for the same idea

items.text: Plain framing: imagine a reviewer following a checklist. They need to see what came in, what was considered, what was rejected, and why the final answer is safe to use.
Technical framing: imagine a trace. It should expose inputs, state, external evidence, model or algorithm output, validation result, and owner for exceptions.

blocks.title: Case study: what changed after the first review

spans.text: The first prototype works on the demo path. Then a reviewer runs the uncomfortable case: the final answer looks right while the agent took unsafe or wasteful steps. The output still looks confident, which is exactly why the lesson needs a richer artifact.

The team does not restart from scratch. It adds one missing control to agent workflow evaluation trace with step-level assertions: a stricter input contract, better source metadata, a validation assertion, a human-review edge, a rollback trigger, or an audit log depending on where the failure appeared.

items.text: Decision made: keep the thin slice, but block release until the failure is observable and repeatable.
Evidence added: the artifact now shows the input, intermediate evidence, final output, and pass/fail reason.
Metric promoted: task success with correct intermediate actions becomes part of the release gate instead of a dashboard someone checks later.

spans.text: Case-study takeaway: a useful Evaluating Agentic Workflows design makes the wrong answer inspectable before it reaches users.

spans.text: This is where Evaluating Agentic Workflows becomes a decision. The team must choose how much rigor agent workflow evaluation trace with step-level assertions needs before it can be trusted.

The wrong move is to jump straight to the fanciest option. The useful move is to ask which option improves task success with correct intermediate actions while making this failure visible: the final answer looks right while the agent took unsafe or wasteful steps.

blocks.title: How this breaks in practice

spans.text: The failure mode to keep in view is concrete: the final answer looks right while the agent took unsafe or wasteful steps. Use it as a diagnostic lens while reading every design choice.

items.text: Golden cases are too easy and miss the failures users actually report.
An assertion checks wording but not the required behavior or source.
The release gate averages away a serious failure in a high-risk slice.
The broad warning sign: task success with correct intermediate actions gets worse even though the final answer or artifact still looks polished.

spans.text: Debugging rule: inspect the earliest place where bad evidence can enter and the latest place where validation should have stopped it.

blocks.useWhen: Use the production path when task success with correct intermediate actions affects users, trust, safety, cost, or compliance.
blocks.avoidWhen: Avoid advanced optimization while the team still cannot reproduce or detect: the final answer looks right while the agent took unsafe or wasteful steps.
blocks.ruleOfThumb: Make the failure visible before making the system more sophisticated.

For agent workflow evaluation trace with step-level assertions, the sketch should prove one thing: the system can improve task success with correct intermediate actions without hiding the failure where the final answer looks right while the agent took unsafe or wasteful steps.
Predict before the code: should the system answer, retrieve more evidence, block, escalate, or mark the case inconclusive when this failure appears?
